instruction:

- In the default (decimal) mode naturalsize no longer prints a trailing ".0" for a whole-number value: naturalsize(3000000) returns "3 MB" instead of "3.0 MB".

- The trailing-".0" removal is general rather than limited to the two quoted inputs: any naturalsize result (default format) whose number would print as N.0 is printed as N, for every unit in both decimal and binary modes, without touching zeros of the integer part.
- The decision is based on the printed (rounded) one-decimal value, not on the raw value being an exact integer: a size that rounds to a whole number at one decimal place also loses the ".0", e.g. naturalsize(1040000) returns "1 MB" (currently "1.0 MB") and naturalsize(2999999) returns "3 MB" (currently "3.0 MB").

The following existing behaviour must be preserved:
- When the one-decimal number has a non-zero decimal digit, naturalsize output is unchanged and keeps its single decimal place: "2.9 KiB" (e.g. naturalsize(3000, binary=True)) stays exactly "2.9 KiB" - it is neither rounded to a whole number nor given extra digits.
